additional_context:
[Council feedback on the previous definition]
From model_reviewer:
- authoring_response.proposed_definition.kinematic_profile.primary_joint_actions[scapulothoracic_joint/downward_rotation]: Downward rotation is a minor scapular motion that accompanies the pull. It is not a load-driving action, yet it is counted at full weight. This promotes levator_scapulae (0.7) and rhomboid_major (0.8) to primary movers. Levator scapulae is not a primary mover in a band-assisted pull-up, so the tracer profile is materially distorted. Suggested correction: Mark scapulothoracic_joint/downward_rotation as emphasis "assist" so rhomboid_major and levator_scapulae become synergists (about 0.32 and 0.28). Keep glenohumeral adduction/extension, elbow flexion and scapular depression as the primary actions.
[End of council feedback]

assumptions: Both hands grip the bar with a pronated (overhand), medium-to-wide grip, as seen in the frames.
The movement is performed for repetitions with controlled lowering and no swinging or kipping, as the instructions state.
One bent knee rests passively in the band loop, which only offsets body weight. The legs perform no meaningful joint action.
Scapular downward rotation accompanies the pull and is marked as assist, following the council feedback.
Both arms perform every action equally, so all actions use the working side and no limb is one-sided.
classification_reasons: The exercise is a bilateral vertical pull from a bar hang. Its joint actions fit the available vocabulary.
The band only reduces the load carried by the legs. The band-knee contact is passive, so the leg does not need to be modeled as a working limb.
The contact sheet shows an overhand grip on a fixed bar, with the body hanging in the first frame and the chin near the bar in the second. This agrees with the instructions.
